newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count steady at 966 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count steady at 966 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 966 as of June 27, unchanged from the prior week and 189 above the year-ago total of 777, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by four to 820, while rigs working offshore rose five to 122. The number of rigs active in inland waters dipped one to 24.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was down by 11 and Oklahoma which was up by seven.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count rose one to 118.

A total of 392 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up 45 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by two to 572, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects dipped by one to two.
There were 215 rigs drilling directionally, 65 drilling horizontally and 686 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs fell by 26 to 321, versus 205 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
